Verdict ready to write (not yet written): the run is unhealthy. Held-out pass rate falls and does not recover: val 6.0% → 2.3% at the first post-update eval (eval 4) and ends at 4.0%; test 7.8% → 1.9% then ends at 4.3%. The same checkpoint’s generated behavior collapses: median response length 7 tokens and ~1.5 turns at rollout 5 / eval 4, truncation near zero, so the model is emitting very short actions (often a single short command or an invalid/done stop), not being cut off by the 2048 budget. Later generations lengthen somewhat (eval medians 37–70) but pass rate stays below the start. Training reward stays ~1–6% and is not evidence of health.

Causal chain (code now confirmed, including mask-weighted reduction):
- Root mechanism: multi-turn tokens include non-trainable observation turns inside `response_length` and the value/reward tensors. PPO adds the episode reward only on the final response token (`loss.py` ~777), which is often a masked observation token if the episode continued past the last assistant turn, or the last assistant token if the episode ended on done/invalid. GAE with gamma=lambd=1 then sets every token’s return equal to that scalar. Policy and value losses are multiplied by loss_mask, so observation tokens get no direct gradient, but their values still enter the backward GAE and therefore the advantages of earlier trainable assistant tokens.
- With reward mostly 0, any positive value on a later token (including a masked observation token) produces a negative advantage on earlier assistant tokens: advantage = R − V = −V when R=0. After only 3 critic-only rollouts the value head (fresh linear head on the reloaded base backbone; Stage A critic state is not what Stage B uses) is still miscalibrated (value loss still ~5.3–7.6; values at rollout 3 ≈ +0.11 vs return 0.06; rollout 5 values 0.42 vs return 0.016, advantages −0.41). The first joint updates (actor steps 6–11, grad norms 14–57, lr 2e-6 constant, kl-coef 0, no reference model) therefore push probability mass off the long trajectories. The first fully on-policy batch after those updates (rollout 5; rollout 4 is still partly from the pre-update policy mixed with the first weight push) is already short and low-reward; eval 4 confirms the same collapse on held-out val and test (median length 7, pass rate 2.3% / 1.9%).
- High initial value loss (~7) is the same order as Stage A before any reload and then declines, so “critic diverged during warmup” is not the cause. The short warmup (3 rollouts / 6 steps) is part of why the value estimates used for the first policy update are still ~0.1–0.4 while returns are ~0.02–0.06. No KL anchor lets the policy move far. Entropy did not collapse; train/rollout logprob mismatch stayed small (~0.01); truncation did not rise; reward function is a real pytest 0/1 and raw_reward matches rewards.
- The loss-mask finding tightens, rather than reverses, the earlier hypothesis: the value loss being large during warmup is computed only on trainable tokens, so it is a real miscalibration of V on the tokens that receive policy gradient, not an artifact of scoring observation tokens. GAE still walks through the masked positions.

Symptoms, not causes: declining value loss after the collapse (easier short trajectories and a value head fitting sparse 0/1 returns), high critic grad norm at init, clipfrac alternating 0/nonzero (two steps per rollout), low training reward, `/abort_request` 200s, modelopt/transformers version warning, truncated log lines in grep, parser `rewards[:50]` cap, Stage A vs Stage B rollout-count difference, short responses after the collapse.

Alternative hypotheses rejected: truncation/budget (trunc ratio falls as pass rate falls); repetition loops (frac 0); reward bug always returning 0 (nonzero pass rate and matching raw_reward); log truncation as proof of crash (series completes through rollout 29, step 59, eval 29); train-only overfitting that hides a healthy eval (eval itself drops); critic reload from base model as an automatic defect by itself (by design; the damage shows up when the actor is updated with the still-miscalibrated advantages under GAE that includes masked tokens and kl-coef 0).

The prior claim that masked observation values corrupt earlier advantages is incorrect. With gamma and lambd both set to one, those intermediate values cancel out in the GAE recursion. Every token receives the same advantage equal to the scalar reward minus its own value. The logs confirm this: rollout/returns equals raw_reward for every token.

The miscalibrated value head is the true root cause. Because the value head is poorly calibrated, its estimates are far too high relative to the scalar reward. When the reward is 0.016 and the value estimate is 0.42, the advantage becomes negative. Policy gradient then decreases the probability of the actions that were actually taken. Most of those actions are failures, so the policy learns to avoid them. This explains the collapse.

The policy gradient update is advantage times ratio times gradient of log probability. Because the value head overestimates, every failed trajectory receives a negative advantage. The policy therefore learns to avoid both long and short trajectories that fail.

When all samples in a batch share similar negative advantages, the policy update shifts probability mass away from the current behavior toward whatever was not sampled. This is especially destructive for a peaked policy.

arguments.content:
# Verdict: unhealthy

Stage B finished the scheduled 30 rollouts (Ray job `raysubmit_Fg68vZaepcLhwdKU` succeeded; actor and critic checkpoints saved at iteration 29; final eval logged). Held-out pass rate fell and never recovered. Before any Stage B update, eval 0 is val 0.060 (300 samples) and test 0.0783 (1200 samples), with median generated length 122.5. After the first joint updates, eval 4 is val 0.0233 and test 0.0192, median length 7 on both splits. Eval 29 ends at val 0.040 and test 0.0433, still below the start, with medians 63 and 70. Training reward stays in the same 1–6% band (rollout 3: 0.0625; rollout 5: 0.0156; rollout 29: 0.0391) and does not show a healthy policy.

## Root cause

The actor is updated, with no KL anchor, on PPO advantages from a value head that is still badly miscalibrated.

Stage B loads the actor from the Stage A Megatron checkpoint (`/ckpt/actor`, iteration 1) and the critic backbone from the base Hugging Face model (`/models/Qwen3-1.7B`). The critic `output_layer` is a fresh `LinearForLastLayer` of shape `[1, hidden]`, initialized `N(0, init_method_std=0.02)`. The HF loader skips that weight because the HF `lm_head` is vocab-sized (`hf_to_megatron/common.py`), so the value head is never copied from Stage A or from the base model. With hidden size 2048, a typical residual, and std 0.02, initial V is O(1). Returns are the episode pytest score, 0 or 1. Squared error of that scale is exactly the observed warmup value loss: critic steps 0–5 are 7.20, 7.65, 6.59, 6.33, 5.42, 5.32, with grad norms 388 down to 235. The same opening scale appears in Stage A (value loss 6.89, 7.03, 6.53, 6.23), which also starts a fresh value head. This is an untrained head, not a diverging one: the loss then falls monotonically in order of magnitude to 0.096 at critic step 59.

`--num-critic-only-steps 3` freezes the actor for rollouts 0–2 (6 critic steps at batch 128 / global batch 64). Joint PPO starts at rollout 3, while value loss is still ~4.7 and the mask-weighted mean value on trainable tokens is +0.108 against a mean return of 0.0625 (advantages −0.046). `--kl-coef 0` and `ref_load None` mean there is no reference penalty. `--entropy-coef 0`, `--normalize-advantages False`, constant lr 2e-6. Actor steps 6–7 have grad norms 19.4 and 14.6. Rollout 4, the first batch from the updated weights, already shortens (generated mean 99, median 51.5, 3.02 turns, reward 0.055) and its advantages flip positive (+0.233) because values have swung to −0.178. Actor step 8 then takes grad norm 57.0. Rollout 5 and eval 4 collapse together: generated mean ~30–36, median 7, about 1.5 turns, train reward 0.0156, values +0.422, advantages −0.406.

With `--gamma 1 --lambd 1`, GAE assigns the same return (the scalar 0/1 reward) to every response token, so `advantage = R − V` on the trainable assistant tokens. Most episodes have R = 0, so any positive V is a negative advantage on the tokens the policy just produced. The first updates therefore decrease the probability of the long multi-turn actions that eval 0 was still emitting. Later updates fit the shorter distribution; held-out pass rate stays below the start through eval 29.

## Symptoms, not causes

- Value loss declining from ~7 to ~0.1, and critic grad norm falling from ~400, are the head fitting sparse 0/1 returns after the policy has already shortened. They match an untrained head, including Stage A before any reload.
- `value_clipfrac` alternating 0 and nonzero is the two optimizer steps per rollout: the first step moves V by more than `--value-clip 0.2`, the second is inside the clip.
- Train reward of a few percent is the base rate of the pytest verifier (`et/sandbox.py` `score`: returncode 0 → 1.0 else 0.0). `raw_reward` equals `rewards` on every logged rollout. It is not evidence of held-out health.
- Truncation is not the collapse. Eval truncation is 0.003 (val) and 0.018 (test) at eval 0 and ~0 at eval 4, while the 2048 response budget is unchanged. Repetition fraction is 0 throughout. Train/rollout logprob abs diff stays ~0.006–0.013, so this is not a train/infer mismatch. Entropy stays ~0.05–0.10. `/abort_request` is slime aborting in-flight episodes at the end of a rollout; the job then completes.
- Placing the reward on the last response token, which may be a non-trainable observation (`et/rollout.py` appends observations with `trainable=False`; `loss.py` does `token_level_rewards[-1] += reward`), does not change the advantages here. Gamma = lambda = 1 makes every token's return equal to the scalar reward whether or not GAE walks through masked positions. Policy and value losses are mask-weighted, so observation tokens get no direct gradient.
- The log is complete through eval 29. A truncated grep view of it is not a defect.
